content.title: Are banks, post offices open on Good Friday? Here's what to know in MS
content.text: April 2, 2026, 1:07 p.m. CTEaster is on Sunday, April 5. That makes April 3 Good Friday.Good Friday marks the day Christians believe Jesus died on the cross. According to the Bible, he was sacrificed to pay for the sins of mankind and his body was later laid to rest in a nearby tomb.Some workplaces will have a three-day weekend, starting with Good Friday, to celebrate Easter. Will you get a day off?The Christian holiday never lands on the same date two years in a row. It can move by more than a month, reshaping the entire spring calendar.Christmas always falls on Dec. 25, but some religious holidays aren't tied to one date. Movable feasts change every year. Some depend on which denomination is celebrating.Here's what to know about banks, mail and shipping options on Good Friday 2026.Are post offices open on Good Friday? Will I get mail?Mail and packages will be delivered. The U.S. Postal Service will deliver as usual, and post offices are open.Will FedEx and UPS deliver packages on Good Friday?FedEx and FedEx Freight will have modified service, according to its holiday calendar.UPS will all run as normal.Are banks open on Good Friday?Most banks will have regular business hours, but you might want to confirm with your local branch.Is the stock market open on Good Friday?The Nasdaq and the New York Stock Exchange are closed for the holiday.Is Good Friday a federal holiday? Will I be off work?Good Friday is not a federal holiday, per a calendar from the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. The next federal holiday is Memorial Day on May 26.Is Good Friday a state holiday in Mississippi?It's also not a state holiday in Mississippi. The next one is Confederate Memorial Day on the last Monday in April, according to the Mississippi Department of Finance and Administration.Check with your workplace and your child's school calendars to see if Good Friday will be a day off for you or your family.Contributing: Chris Sims, Marina Johnson and John TuftsBonnie Bolden is the Deep South Connect reporter for Mississippi with USA TODAY NETWORK. Email her at bbolden@gannett.com.
